selected.rationale: Kill of the auxiliary user-mention service propagates through the text service into compose-post, turning optional mention enrichment into a hard blocker for post creation. Exposes an architecture-level coupling defect on the hidden text->user-mention dependency with no fallback/isolation.

Kill of the URL-shortening service similarly takes down compose-post through the text-processing path; optional URL enrichment becomes a hard dependency. Confirms missing dependency isolation/fallback for a side service.

Loss on compose-post->home-timeline makes the home-timeline write fan-out fail; the post may already be stored, so the request errors after the 10s timeout and leaves a partial write with duplicate risk on retry. Affects the critical compose-post->home-timeline write edge.

Loss on home-timeline->social-graph prevents building home timelines because the follower graph is unavailable; the synchronous call has no degraded-mode fallback, so reads fail or time out. Exposes missing loss handling on a core read fan-out edge.

Loss on compose-post->post-storage prevents the post from being persisted; with no evident retry, a transient storage failure becomes a guaranteed post-creation failure. Core persistence edge exposed.

Loss on compose-post->user-timeline occurs after post-storage persistence, leaving a stored post that is absent from the author's timeline; no compensating transaction is present. Exposes partial-write inconsistency on the user-timeline edge.
Loss on compose-post->unique-id aborts post creation at the first dependency; without retry, a transient ID-service failure is directly visible to users. Affects the compose-post->unique-id edge.

Delay on home-timeline->post-storage adds direct latency to every home-timeline read and is only capped by the 10s timeout, producing multi-second user-facing delays. Demonstrates latency propagation on the read path.

Kill of the home-timeline service removes both the write fan-out used by compose-post and the read path for home timelines; recovery depends solely on pod restart with no redundant instance. Confirms availability/recovery weakness.

Kill of the compose-post service takes down the single orchestrator for all post creation; no replica failover means a total write outage until restart. Availability/recovery weakness at the core writer.
